recipes.name: Easy Slow Cooker Sweet and Sour Pork Chops

steps.text: Heat a large skillet over high heat. Add pork chops and sear until browned, 1 to 2 minutes per side. Transfer to a slow cooker.

Mix brown sugar, ketchup, onion, and lemon juice together in a bowl; spoon over pork chops. Cover and cook on Low until pork chops are very tender, 4 to 6 hours. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Slow Cooker Sweet and Sour Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: These sweet and sour pork chops are easy to make in your slow cooker with basic pantry staples of brown sugar, ketchup, onion, and a bit of lemon juice.

review.reviewBody: Nice flavor and very easy. I used more chopped onions, added fresh pressed garlic, added a "glob of peach preserves, substituted apple cider vinegar for the lemon, and added bell pepper chunks and sliced canned pineapple (both near the end). I thickened the sauce to use as gravy over rice. Next time I will cut the onions in big chunks and add red food coloring for a more traditional looking dish. I love the ease of using a crock pot. I will make this often. Thanks.

Definately a keeper ! I added chunks of red and yellow peppers and chunks of onions and thickened the sauce with corn starch before serving over rice. I also baked it in the oven at 300 for a couple of hours as I didn't' have time to cook it in the slow cooker. You could cut the chops with your fork. Yumm!

Very tasty. Cut the pork into bite size pieces. I used apple cider vinegar instead of the lemon juice. Added a dole snack size pineapple bowl with the juice, sweet peppers, and garlic powder. During last 30 minutes of cooking , removed some of the juice and mixed it with 2 T. corn starch and stirred it into the slow cooker with the other ingredients. During the last 10 minutes, added a package of snow peas.

This recipe is fantastic. I used a thinner pork chop cut and only marinated the chops for 1.5 - 2.0 hours. I substituted rice wine vinegar and used maple smoke mesquite spice. I grilled them only 4 minutes--using the method the internet recommended. Grill on high 1 minute with lid down; turn 45 degrees, lid down for another minute. Then turn chops and repeat. Chops were succulent and juicy with a lot of flavor. This is the best recipe for pork chops I've ever had.

Very easy and delicious, even the picky eaters in my house loved it. I only give it 4 stars because I did have to make some changes. I followed the advice of other reviews and doubled the sauce, it still didn't look like enough so I added more, and it still could have had more sauce. I also added a yellow and orange pepper, and an onion and a half instead of the 2 tbs that it called for. I also watched it very closely and only cooked it for 3 hours on low, I think that 4-6 hours is way too long. Thanks for a great recipe!

I made this last night on the stove top and it was a hit! Very simple and tasty. I did saute onions & garlic first and substitued apple cider vinegar for lemon. Needed extra liquid so I added a little beef broth. Served on buttered rice with sweet peas. It will diffently be a frequent meal for my family. Thanks for sharing the recipe.
I added small jar maraschino cherries [drained] & small can pineapple tidbits [drained]. omitted ketchup.

I snagged a lot of others ideas....... added onion, peppers, used the juice of a small can of pineapple and added the pineapple the last 3o minutes. used 1/2 catsup and 1/2 barbecue sauce (doubled the sauce) but added a couple of heaping tablesppons of hot pepper jelly (omitted the brown sugar) It was perfect over white rice. My husband was very reluctant to try it......... but he finished off a big bowl. If the sauce is too thin, just add cornstarch mixed with water. The hot pepper jelly adds a nice kick! :-)

This is a great, easy recipe. I followed other reviewers' suggestions and doubled the sauce. I also added 1 tbsp of pineapple juice to the sauce and added pineapple chumks and chopped green bell pepper at the end.

Yummy - I added minced garlic and heated the onion and garlic just long enough to take the rawness out - but the recipe probably doesn't need this step. Tip: dry chops on paper towel before searing - and I used paper towel to suck up any fat on chops after they were seared.

This recipe is a real good starting point, but as much as I changed, I should probably start a new recipe. Based on other people's comments, I tripled the original recipe for the same 4 pork chops (large, bone in chops), in addition, I added 4 tablespoons of pineapple juice from a can of crushed pineapples. I also used chopped raw onion. In the last hour, I added the crushed pineapple and chopped green pepper. I had plenty of juice and served everything over egg noodles instead of rice. I thought it turned out really well, but it's pretty different.

I used 3 bone-in pork chops and a whole largely diced onion for this recipe. I cooked it for nearly 6 hours. Yes, the pork was a bit dry, it IS pork chop, BUT the sauce really helped it. I basted the chops every couple of hours or so too. I sauteed 2 green bell peppers and served this over 1 cup (uncooked I mean,) rice. Put on some soy sauce, sesame seeds and sriacha sauce. Quite good! I would totally make it again and add canned pineapple. (Also, with the rice and bell peppers, it made 4 servings. I can't see how it could be without.)

Husband and I loved it..14 year old not so much... I adjusted the recipe...I doubled the sauce but only did 1/4 c of brown sugar and 1/8 c of brown sugar..I added diced red peppers and finely chopped some orange rind..probably about 1/2 a small orange. Cooked it in the crockpot on high 6 hours...added the red pepper and finely chopped orange rind with about 2 hours before serving. I served it over rice...just wish it had more veggies in it.
The only thing I did differently was to double all ingredients to make more sauce..was an easy and delicious meal.

This was a simple dinner and delicious! Only different addition was I added sweet peppers an hour before it was done . Oh and I did double the sauce as other reviewers suggested. We had this served over brown rice,wonderful sauce! Thank you
Excellent flavor. I did add green pepper and pineapple. Slow cooked center cut loin chops and served with rice. I will definitely make again.
I don’t often make pork chops for my family but this recipe that has become a favorite and is requested at least once a week. It was amazing!
Made just as the recipe stated to, except used a roast and not chops. Turned out really good, tender, juicy, and great flavor. Next time I'll add pineapple and bell peppers.

I don't know why everyone thinks you have to cook pork to death. Decent chops are done in 3-4 minutes, shoulder steaks take a bit longer and have more flavor if cooked well done, I prefer shoulder meat when it's braised for 15-20 minutes, but to cook them for 4-5 hours is ridiculous.
Good, tasty, nice change.
